title: Tanker Crashes Into Cruise Ship on the Mississippi
summary: A giant tanker lost its steering on the Mississippi River on Friday and crashed into a docked river cruise ship in New Orleans. The crash left the cruise ship on its side and sent about 100 people into the river, but everyone survived. The tanker, the Atlantic Asphalt, is 520 feet long. It appeared to lose steering, Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said, and the exact cause is not yet known. All 197 passengers and crew survived. Thirty-two people were taken to hospital. Passengers wore life vests on the third deck when the ship rolled, sending Joe Knab and about 100 others into the river. The water was 66 degrees Fahrenheit, and Knab said he was in it for about 15 minutes. The port says the tanker caused at least 1 million dollars in damage. The National Transportation Safety Board has recovered the voyage data recorder and sent a 16-member team to investigate for a week. Moving the cruise ship could take weeks, and its 16,000 gallons of fuel must be removed safely first.
why_it_matters: If you ever ride a boat or cruise ship, wearing a life vest and knowing what to do in an emergency can help keep you safe if something goes wrong.

keywords.explanation: A tanker is a very large ship that carries liquids in big tanks.
Steering is controlling which way a ship or vehicle turns.
Docked means a ship is stopped and tied up at a port.
Life vests are jackets that help a person float in water.
A voyage data recorder is a device that records what happened on a ship.
To investigate is to look closely to find out what happened and why.
